correctness.finding: PASS. The six-cell proof survives independent reconstruction. For an infinite common-zero direction, choosing the part of the denominator coprime to 6 leaves a common nontrivial root of unity for every parallel section, so every nonempty section has size at least two and the only six-point profiles are (3,3), (2,4), or (2,2,2). Two 3-profiles are impossible by intersection counting; a 3-profile with an even profile forces a full 2×3 grid, and full affine span makes the grid coordinates unimodular with one-dimensional factors of sizes 2 and 3 and gcd-one spans. The unequal-prime product lemma then gives an axis period. Two even profiles reduce either to the same forbidden grid count or, in the (2,2,2)/(2,2,2) case, to K_{3,3} minus a perfect matching; the three two-term root equations contradict n_13=n_12+n_23. In the complementary spectral case, Khetan's published Case (2) uses only the dilation equations, finite exceptional support, irrational character values, and the integer-valued exponential-sum lemma; inspection of the full open preprint confirms that this branch does not use |F|=p^2 beyond indexing dilations by integers coprime to |F|. Replacing 'coprime to p' by 'coprime to 6' is therefore valid.
